drills.q: An AR(1) has phi=0.95 and innovation sigma=1. What is the variance after 20 steps vs the unconditional variance?
drills.a: RW-like accumulation: Var_n = n*sigma^2 would be 20 if phi=1; for phi=0.95, Var_h = sigma^2*(1-phi^(2h))/(1-phi^2) = (1-0.358)/(0.0975) ~ 6.6, saturating toward unconditional 1/(1-0.9025) ~ 10.3. Mean reversion caps uncertainty.

drills.q: ADF t-stat on a monthly series is -2.4 (constant-only spec). Verdict at 5%?
drills.a: FAIL to reject: -2.4 > -2.86 critical value. Treat as unit-root-suspect. But check power: pair with KPSS (H0 stationarity) and inspect ACF decay before concluding - persistent stationary series routinely produce such values.

drills.q: You difference a trend-stationary series and its acf[1] becomes -0.48 with a fitted MA(1) theta = -0.92. Diagnose.
drills.a: Classic overdifferencing: differencing an already-stationary (around deterministic trend) series induces an artificial MA(1) near the invertibility boundary and inflates variance. Detrend instead of difference, or use d=0 with a trend regressor.

drills.q: ACF decays geometrically; PACF cuts off after lag 3. Propose orders and your first alternative candidates.
drills.a: AR(3). Fit neighbors AR(2)/AR(4) plus ARMA(2,1)-style competitors, choose by AIC/BIC, then verify residuals pass Ljung-Box. Plot signatures propose; information criteria confirm.

drills.q: Estimate the small-sample bias of an AR(1) coefficient with true phi=0.8 from T=50 observations (Hurwicz approximation).
drills.a: Bias ~ -(1+3phi)/T = -(1+2.4)/50 = -0.068. Expected estimate ~0.73 instead of 0.80 - material at short samples; use MLE or bootstrap bias correction.

drills.q: Two independent random-walk price series regressed levels-on-levels give slope t=4.1, R^2=0.94, DW=0.31. Interpret.
drills.a: Textbook spurious regression: DW << R^2 (Granger-Newbold heuristic), huge R^2 from shared trending, t meaningless because statistics diverge under unit-root nulls. Difference both or test cointegration via error-correction modeling; never trade this 'relationship'.

drills.q: For AR(2) phi=(0.6,-0.2), verify stationarity via the triangle inequalities.
drills.a: phi1+phi2=0.4<1 ok; phi2-phi1=-0.8<1 ok; |phi2|=0.2<1 ok. Stationary. Roots of z^2-0.6z+0.2 are complex conjugates (discriminant 0.36-0.8<0): damped pseudo-cycle with period 2*pi/angle.

drills.q: Monthly revenue shows growing amplitude December spikes plus upward drift. Give the transformation sequence and candidate model.
drills.a: log() to stabilize multiplicative seasonality -> ADF/KPSS on logs vs log-diffs -> typically d=1, D=1 at m=12 -> fit airline ARIMA(0,1,1)(0,1,1)_12 first; add trading-day/holiday regressors (SARIMAX) if calendar-irregular. Validate against seasonal-naive MASE on a held-out year.

drills.q: Why does Ljung-Box p=0.85 on residuals not prove model adequacy?
drills.a: The same data selected orders minimizing autocorrelation, so residual whiteness is partly guaranteed by construction (post-selection optimism); DF should shrink by p+q. Supplement with out-of-sample walk-forward error, ACF inspection at seasonal lags, and stability checks across windows.
